title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 67 (Restrictions on financial assistance for purchase of own shares)

content.overview: Section 67 restricts a company from giving financial assistance for the purchase of or subscription to its own shares or those of its holding company, subject to the section's scope and exceptions.
content.glance: Section 67 restricts a company from giving financial assistance for the purchase of or subscription to its own shares or those of its holding company, subject to the section's scope and exceptions.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 67 (Restrictions on purchase by company or giving of loans by it for purchase of its shares). Section 67 restricts financial assistance for the purchase of or subscription to shares in the company or its holding company. The analysis must identify the company type, purpose and connection of the assistance, the applicable subsection, and any statutory exception. The section includes exceptions relating to banking-company lending in the ordinary course and qualifying employee share arrangements/loans, subject to their conditions. A private-company exemption may depend on the conditions in the applicable Central Government notification; do not assume a blanket exemption. Distinguish this assistance restriction from a company buy-back under section 68 and director-loan rules under section 185. Verify the current statutory text and notifications before applying an exception. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Prohibited assistance
sections.body: Identify whether the company provides financial assistance for the purpose of or in connection with the purchase of or subscription to shares in the company or its holding company. Apply the scope of section 67 to the particular company and transaction.

sections.heading: Statutory exceptions
sections.body: The section contains specified exceptions, including ordinary-course lending by a banking company and qualifying employee share arrangements or loans. Each exception has its own statutory conditions; do not generalise beyond its wording.

sections.heading: Private-company exemption
sections.body: Any reliance on a private-company exemption must be tied to the conditions of the applicable Central Government notification in force for the relevant period. Do not treat private companies as universally exempt without checking those conditions.

sections.heading: Separate provisions
sections.body: Section 67 addresses financial assistance connected with share acquisition. Section 68 governs a company's buy-back; section 185 is a separate restriction on loans to directors and connected persons.

examples.title: Employee scheme
examples.body: Money provided under a qualifying employee scheme for fully paid shares can fall within the exception.

examples.title: Routed loan
examples.body: A loan to a relative of a promoter to buy the company's shares can be indirect assistance.

hypotheticals.question: A company proposes to fund an employee share arrangement. What must be checked under section 67?
hypotheticals.analysis: Confirm that the arrangement falls within the specific employee exception and satisfies the statutory approval, beneficiary and instrument conditions. Do not rely on the label 'employee scheme' alone.

hypotheticals.question: A private company gives financial assistance connected with a share purchase. Is it automatically exempt?
hypotheticals.analysis: No blanket exemption should be assumed. Check the applicable Central Government notification and each condition in force for the relevant period.

distinctions.title: Financial assistance and buy-back
distinctions.left: Section 67 concerns financial assistance connected with purchase or subscription of shares.
distinctions.right: Section 68 governs the company's own purchase of its shares or specified securities.

rows.right: Company buys back its own securities

misconceptions.trap: Assuming every private company is automatically outside section 67.
misconceptions.correction: Verify the applicable exemption notification and all conditions before relying on it.

misconceptions.trap: Treating any employee-related loan as exempt.
misconceptions.correction: Apply the exact conditions of the statutory employee exception, including the relevant approval and beneficiary limits.

misconceptions.trap: Confusing financial assistance with a company's own buy-back.
misconceptions.correction: Section 67 addresses assistance connected with share acquisition; section 68 governs the company's buy-back.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: Whether the company gives financial assistance for purchase of or subscription to its own shares or those of its holding company, and whether a specific statutory exception or applicable notification applies.
